stable.notes: Quick save, capture stall recovery, speaker ID on by default for Mac recordings, and iPhone microphone meetings. Pairs with COS server 6.93.0.

whatsNew.summary: Stopping a Mac recording now shows Saving, then Saved, and a short COS hiccup is retried for you. A recording that stops receiving audio is restarted, and Recover checks the server first. Speaker ID is on by default for Mac recordings, and you can assign a Voice to a person in your voice profiles. You can record meetings from your iPhone microphone once your server enables it. Plus everything in 0.5.350: Usage date ranges and provider trends, and smoother Windu running.

items: Stopping a Mac recording shows Saving, then Saved. The chunk counter, the retained-recording warning and Retry no longer appear during an ordinary save, which takes about 5 seconds.

If a save runs past 20 seconds, the panel says how far it got. If COS misses a beat right after Stop, Control tries again quietly for about a minute. Only then does it say Not saved yet, Audio is safe on this Mac, and offer Retry.

Before Meetings offers to recover a retained Mac recording, Control asks the server whether it already saved it. If it did, the row goes away and the local copy is marked saved. If the server cannot answer, the row stays.
A grayed-out Recover button now says why, such as Recover is available after this recording, or once this recording is saved.
If a Mac recording stops receiving audio for about 30 seconds, the panel says so and Control restarts the capture once. If that fails, Stop and save keeps everything up to then.

Audio is written to disk on its own thread, so a busy or frozen Control window no longer drops the recording. Quitting Control with a termination signal during a recording keeps every saved chunk, and the recording shows up ready to save on the next launch.
Meetings recorded from your iPhone microphone appear in Live now, Meetings and Today as iPhone microphone. You stop them on the iPhone, where Control shows Stop on iPhone instead of a stop button.
Every line from an iPhone recording reads Speaker. Naming, merging, Save all and speaker settings are off for these recordings.

iPhone recording is off until you turn it on in your server settings and use a COS Glasses companion that offers it. It records the iPhone microphone only, not audio playing on the phone such as Zoom, YouTube or calls.

On a Mac recording, pick a person already in your voice profiles for a Voice and Control previews how many voice samples it would add and how well the voice matches. If it does not match, holds more than one voice or has too little audio, Save is replaced by Rename only, the default, and a separate Add anyway that asks once more. Your own profile is not offered. Samples added this way are capped at 10, never exceed the person's other samples, and are the first to go when other samples need room. A typed name still renames text only.
Pairs with COS server 6.93.0. Speaker ID is on by default for Mac recordings: Voice 1 and Voice 2 appear as you record. Set COS_MAC_LIVE_VOICES=off on the server to turn it off.

Known limit: when one person hands over to another exactly at a chunk boundary, the new speaker can be given the previous speaker's number, and the saved meeting keeps the live numbers. A Voice is a number, never a name, until you assign it.
Compare Last 7, 30 or 90 days, a completed weekend, custom dates or all history. Charts and totals follow the same filters.
Choose provider or model series, lines or stacked bars. Inspect a period for its breakdown, and compare provider totals, token categories and daily records.
Usage records are not sessions. Token share and estimated API value do not measure your subscription allowance; missing prices and coverage remain visible.
Windu uses a consistent cadence for both running bursts before his strike. Failed combat-art loads can retry on a later refresh. Custom artwork and settings stay intact.
Hover a Usage bar to see its period and model breakdown. Click to keep it open, or use Inspect period and Previous/Next with the keyboard.
Compare Last weekend or Last 7 days. Selection share and Within provider show their token denominators; neither is your subscription allowance.
Exclude repeated cache reads from token comparisons. Estimated API value stays separate and unknown prices remain visible.
Windu turns his head while idle and moves through meditation poses with a violet power-up aura, alongside illustrated patrol frames.
The thirteen combat casts keep their artwork, timing and handoffs. Previous artwork remains available for rollback.
Exact stock packs update automatically. Custom artwork, timing and scale stay intact. Sessions Usage remains available under Sessions.
Open Sessions, then Usage. Compare a month or All history by provider and model, with input, output and cache tokens shown separately.
Switch between daily usage and monthly history, and between tokens and estimated API value. The model table shows which models account for the most tokens.

COS backfills Claude Code and Codex session records stored on this Mac, including archived Codex sessions and subagents. Large histories import in bounded passes; partial totals and coverage gaps are shown.
Usage history stays on this Mac and survives deletion of previously imported session logs. Pause tracking at any time. COS stores counts and model names, not conversation text.

Cost is a standard API-equivalent estimate, not your subscription bill. It applies the October 25 rate snapshot to all dates. Unknown prices stay unavailable; browser-only sessions, Cursor and other Macs are not included.
Longer custom pet animations retain their approved timing, including 256-frame casts. Your installed artwork is preserved.
Includes 0.5.345 dictation improvements and its fix for learning edits to capitalized dictations.
Jedi Miles Windu gains thirteen illustrated combat casts across Sessions 1–4. Exact stock packs update; custom artwork and playback settings stay yours.

COS leaves out um, uh, er and hmm said on their own before it types or copies, also with AI polish off. Text in another language, file names such as um.py, and handles such as @uh keep them. Settings, Dictation, Remove filler sounds turns it off. What was heard stays on the card.

A dictation at the start of a text box, or after a full stop, question mark or new line, starts with a capital when COS can read the text box. Never in terminals or password fields, and never for words like iPhone, @handles, paths or a lowercase word in your dictionary. Settings, Dictation, Capitalize the start of a sentence.

When you are still holding ⌘ or ⌃ as Claude's polish arrives, COS waits up to 1.2 seconds for you to let go, then a moment of no typing, before it swaps the polished text in. Shift and Option still count as typing. Settings can turn the wait off.
Undo polish, on the pill after a swap and on the dictation's card, puts back exactly what COS typed. Apply polished in Activity puts Claude's version back again.

Under AI polish, one line says which polish your COS server runs for the model you chose: the newest polish, the earlier one, or Previous polish you picked. COS reads it again when the server is updated or rolled back.

If the microphone fails to start with System default, COS tries a microphone that delivered sound before (never Bluetooth or an iPhone) and says which it used. A sound or a mute that hits an audio error pauses for 10 minutes instead of holding up dictation, with Play sounds again and Mute again in Settings.

When an edit you make is one Claude's polish had already made, the card says so and COS learns nothing from it. Every edited dictation's card now says what happens next time: a word COS will write, a style rule on its way, or nothing to learn.
COS no longer offers to always drop um or uh: those are left out before typing now. One less round trip to the COS server before each dictation.

While Learn from my edits watches a dictation, COS tries to read that text box once more when you press Return or Enter, with or without Shift or Command, or click in that app. Return never ends the watch: sending the text or leaving the field does.

While COS watches your edit, it notices Return, clicks and other key presses in the app it typed into, as counts only. It never records which keys. This needs a single-key dictation shortcut such as Fn.
COS checks for your change sooner after you stop typing. Your dictionary still learns a word only after a longer pause.
If your last change may not have been read before the text was sent or cleared, nothing is saved. COS never keeps an older version as what you sent.

When AI polish gives back your words unchanged, COS records it as unchanged, not as a failed polish. When the server cleaned up filler or spellings on its own, COS still puts the cleaned text in, and the card says Cleaned up.
With COS server 6.91.0, Sonnet now uses the new polish (v4), and its card says so, for example Polished · Sonnet · v4. Previous polish (v3) in Settings, Dictation goes back to the earlier prompt.

With AI polish on Claude Sonnet, COS can learn two style habits from changes you make to text it typed: dropping a filler such as "honestly" or "to be honest", and using or writing out contractions. A habit becomes a rule after you make the same change in two dictations.
Your style rules apply only to Sonnet polish with the new prompt. On Haiku, with Previous polish, or with learning off, Settings lists them as Not used or Paused, and COS learns nothing new.

When COS adds a rule, the pill says Learned your style, with Undo, once for each rule. Settings, Dictation, Your style lists your rules with Remove, lets you add one or reset them, and has a switch to stop learning. Suggest only proposes rules instead of adding them.

Your COS server adds your style rules (never your text) to each Sonnet polish, on G2 too when it polishes with Sonnet. On your Mac, COS keeps only codes and counts for them, and clearing your dictation history clears what it learned.
When the meaning check refuses Claude's version, because polish changed a number, a date, a name, a link or a negation, COS keeps its own cleaned text, and the card says so.

Meetings, Sessions, Tasks, Memories, Threads, Speakers, Messages, a meeting's page, a session and Today's Needs you and Running cards draw the outline of their rows while they load, then fill in with your data.
A Meeting Ask answer draws its outline in the line where it will appear while COS reads the meeting.

Your data shows the moment it arrives, readable and ready to click. Loads that finish quickly show it directly, and a view you already opened this session updates as before. A view whose last load came back empty shows its usual loading line next time, until it has data again; an error is never counted as empty.
If a load takes more than a few seconds, the usual loading words show. Errors and empty results show at once, with the same message and buttons as before.
Nothing changes size while it loads. Reduce Motion turns the outline off, and VoiceOver hears what is loading.
When you change words COS just typed, the pill says Edit saved, with View. If COS also learned a word, it says Edit saved and Learned, with Undo.

The dictation card shows what was sent: removed words struck through, added words underlined, and how many edits you made. Show original shows exactly what COS typed, and Copy copies whichever you are looking at.
One line on the card says whether your edit went to your dictionary, and why not when it did not: COS learns names and terms, not everyday words.

When your only edit was removing a short filler like "kind of", one tap on Always drop adds it to your polish instructions, so AI polish leaves it out next time. Undo takes it back out. Nothing is added unless you tap.
Only edits inside the text COS typed count, in the apps where Learn from my edits works. Your edited text stays on this Mac with the dictation.
Nia, Elara and Rowan each have distinct Session 2 and 3 choreography and a full 360 attack in Session 4, with smoother recovery and guard transitions.
Opponents enter with their blasters ready, react after saber contact, and rotate between three casts without immediately repeating. Flying opponents vary in Session 3.
Sharper Retina artwork includes corrected Nia boots and a guard that keeps her free hand clear of the blade.
Existing unmodified Jedi packs update automatically. Custom artwork, timing, scale and Miles Windu are preserved.
Includes the 0.5.340 Mac Voice 1/Voice 2 labels, text-only Rename voice, and Learn from my edits in Slack. Voice labels require COS server 6.90.0.
With COS server 6.90.0, a saved Mac recording labels its voices Voice 1, Voice 2 and so on. Each voice keeps its number for the whole meeting.
Rename voice on the saved meeting picks a voice and opens it in Speakers to name. The name replaces that voice's turns in this meeting.
Renaming a Mac recording's voice is text only. No voice profile is made or trained from Mac audio.
A call with too many voices, or voices COS cannot tell apart, stays Ext, as before.
Voice 1 and Voice 2 count as two voices to name in Speakers and Today. The Ext left beside them is not counted as one more.
Learn from my edits works in Slack: fix a misheard name in the message COS just typed, and COS learns it, with Undo. Cursor, ChatGPT and rich text boxes in Chrome and Comet are still measured first.
Drop a screenshot or file anywhere on a live meeting. The transcript is outlined with Drop to add to this meeting while you drag.
Add file sits beside Stop in the bar: Paste screenshot (Command-V) or Choose files (Command-O).
Files collapse to one Files row under the title, with the count and size. Open it to Quick Look, show in Finder or remove a file.
The line under the bar is gone, so the transcript has more room.
With COS server 6.87.0, a glasses meeting shows a rough audio level per chunk in the bar, dotted when it was quiet. It runs a few seconds behind the room.
In a narrow window the level shrinks first, Add file becomes just the paperclip, and the buttons stay on one line.
Learn from my edits works in Claude. Fix a misheard name in the text COS just typed, in the same message, and COS learns it.
The pill says Learned and the word, with Undo, for a few seconds. The word also stays in Activity, Dictation, under Learned, with Undo, for 30 days.
COS follows the text box, not one piece of it, so Claude redrawing its message box no longer ends the watch. Sending the message ends it.
If you edit right around your dictation, or while AI polish is still working, COS finds your words again instead of giving up.
It learns names and terms only, at most two from one dictation, and never a fix to a plain English word.
Slack, Cursor, ChatGPT and rich text boxes in Chrome and Comet are measured first, and Settings names them. Learning there comes once a measurement shows it reads the text right.
Nothing COS reads while it watches is saved or sent. Only the word pair it learns goes to your dictionary.
Today's From today's meetings has a Dismiss on each suggestion, beside Create task and Open in Work, for items that are not real tasks, like someone else's follow-up or something already done.
After you dismiss one, the row says Dismissed for about 8 seconds, with Undo on a COS server that has it, then leaves. The count beside From today's meetings and in the rail drops right away.
Undo puts the suggestion back where it was. A dismissed suggestion never shows on Today again and does not move to Work at midnight.
If the server says no, the row stays and shows why. Dismiss uses the same server path as Dismiss in Work, so it needs no server update.
With Full Keyboard Access, press Delete on a focused suggestion to dismiss it. VoiceOver reads each one as Dismiss suggestion and its words.

Work's board shows Queued and From glasses on a card with work waiting in its Work chat, and opens the chat. You get a notice when queued work needs a new plan, or when a plan from your glasses is waiting.
On a COS server without the newer Work routes, Work no longer shows red errors on Sort, hides Expired, and offers Undo only where it works.

Runs started from Today open their own session, have Stop while they run, and come back to Today when they finish. Stop also works on reviewed Work chat rounds and on work waiting in a busy session's queue.
Live cues say which limit stopped them and when it lifts, a missing key opens the key fields in Settings, and saved Mac recordings show their Cues tab.
AI polish says when the server's daily limit or a run of errors paused it. Naming a voice from Today shows Named, with Undo. A full Work chat says it is full.

COS Control uses less of your Mac while idle: the pet stops animating when you can't see it, status checks slow down when no COS window is open or the screen is locked, and resizing Activity no longer rebuilds the whole Today page.
Fix a word stays on screen: its panel never opens past the bottom or the sides of the screen.
Learn from my edits now learns from fixes you make in COS Control's own text boxes, like the Work task editor.
The Work chat's buttons and pickers fit a narrow window: they move to a second row instead of squeezing.
The live meeting window shows the meeting's real title: what you typed for a Mac recording, or your calendar event when it started near the recording.
Under the title, one line says where it records and, with COS server 6.86.0, what the cues found so far, like 2 decisions, 1 promise and 1 follow-up.
A strip shows the voices heard so far, with a small bar under the one heard last. Names arrive with the text, a few seconds after they speak, and a Mac recording never shows You.

With COS server 6.86.0, each cue sits under the part of the conversation it belongs to, marked Decision, Promise, Follow-up, Challenge or Reinforce, with the same five ratings. The Cues tab keeps the full list.
With COS server 6.86.0, the words still being transcribed show in grey under the last line and are replaced by the final text.

A bar at the bottom shows the red dot, the time so far, a live audio level for Mac recordings, and Stop. Command-Shift-R stops a Mac recording and saves it. With Reduce Motion on, the level is a still bar.
Live cues now work on Mac recordings too, with COS server 6.86.0 and Live cues on, under the same limits as the glasses. If the server says no, the window says why and the recording goes on.

The Meetings tab shows a small level and the time while a meeting records. Live COS Ask and the files drop stay where they were: drop in screenshots or files while it's on, and they're saved with the meeting.
Activity has a new Today home, off until you turn on Settings, New Today home. With it off, Activity works as before.
Today shows what is waiting on you first, with your sessions' questions in their own words and one Open for each.

Running lists what every agent is working on, in Terminal, Claude, Codex, Cursor, Work, the glasses and routines, and opens each in the right place. With COS server 6.85.0, questions you ask on your glasses or phone show there while COS answers.
Next up shows your next meeting, and Prep me asks COS for a short brief before it. From today's meetings lists today's suggestions until midnight, with Create task.
A rail beside every Activity tab shows each section in one line. Runs started from Today are capped at 20 a day on this Mac, and quiet hours fold everything but questions after 6 PM and on weekends.

Your polish instructions, in Settings, Dictation, under AI polish: tell AI polish how you like your text, such as Oxford commas or how to write product names, up to 1,000 characters. COS's built-in rules still come first, so your words never change meaning, links, numbers or names.

See the built-in polish rules from the same place. Your instructions are used for Mac and glasses dictation, not meeting transcripts. They need COS server 6.85.0; with an older server the box does not show.
Fix a word accepts a link, email or path as a correction, so you can teach it forward slash pricing written /pricing. COS shows the server's note that it is kept as a correction only.
Saying forward slash pricing in a dictation writes /pricing, with COS server 6.84.0.
Learn from my edits keeps the leading / of a path (and @, #, ~ or .) instead of learning just pricing.

AI polish uses the server's new v3 prompt, which handles spoken links, paths and formatting asks. If the server refuses a polished answer because it holds a link you never said, COS pastes what it heard and does not call it polished.
Record on Mac checks that it can hear your Mac. If All Mac audio gets only digital silence while an app is playing, COS stops within about 12 seconds instead of recording silence for the whole call.

You then see one message: COS Control can't hear your Mac's audio, and macOS may not be letting it record system audio. Open System Settings goes to Screen & System Audio Recording, and Try again starts a fresh recording.
A quiet meeting keeps recording: the check stops only on exact digital silence, never on low sound.

A recording with no sound now offers Discard (no sound was captured), with a confirm, instead of Retry saving or Save, which could not work. Its audio moves to a dated discarded folder on this Mac; nothing is deleted.
With COS server 6.84.0, Discard also clears the server's copy, so it leaves Unsaved captures. With an older server, only this Mac's copy is discarded, and COS says so.
A recording with no sound no longer shows Saved meeting not found yet: there is no meeting to find.
The Work chat finds every session on a card: the ones the card started, the ones you linked, and the ones that report on it. It no longer says no sessions are attached when the card has them.

Before it plans, it reads where each session stopped and how much Claude and Codex usage you have left, so it avoids stale sessions and platforms that are nearly out. It can also start a new session or fork one.
Each card has an Auto-send switch, with the default in Settings, off unless you turn it on. On, the plan goes out without the review click, and every running step has a Stop.

Plans you make on your glasses appear in the card's Work chat marked From glasses. The glasses can send them after a two-step confirm, through the same path as Send here. A plan you already sent from the Mac is never sent twice.
Needs COS server 6.83.0. With an older server, Work chat works as before.
Dictation now pastes into Google Slides, Docs and Sheets in Comet. Comet is now treated like Chrome, so it no longer says No text box.
In Slides, Docs and Sheets, COS can't see where the text lands. With AI polish on, COS waits for Claude there and pastes once, as it did before 0.5.331.

Swapping in Claude's version is safer in apps that take a paste, like Claude, Slack and Chrome. COS replaces the whole dictation, checks the text box again right before it pastes, and skips if you typed, sent or moved.
If a swap may not have landed cleanly, the pill says Check and the app name. Activity, Dictation shows what you said and Claude's version, with Copy polished.
Dictation with AI polish is faster. COS now types what it heard right away, about a second after you let go of the key. When Claude's version is ready, COS swaps it in at the same spot.

COS swaps only when it can prove the text there is still what it typed. In apps that take a paste, like Chrome, Slack and Claude, it swaps only while you are still in that text box. It never brings an app forward or moves you somewhere else.
If COS can't swap, your text stays as it was typed and the pill says so. Open Activity, Dictation and choose Apply polished on that dictation.
To turn it off, go to Settings, Dictation, Paste right away, then polish in place. Off works as before: COS waits for Claude, then pastes once.

Jedi Miles Windu is Version 15: four rotating opponents on one session too, blaster bolts that travel, smoother droid movement, and cleaner art. Your Mac also uses less memory for the pet: only the scene on screen is loaded.

Set how many live cues you get in Settings, Meeting assistant: the bar (lower for more cues, higher for fewer), the most cues in a meeting, the shortest gap between two cues and a daily limit, with today's usage shown underneath. Needs COS server 6.79.2 or later.
With AI polish on, Claude starts getting ready the moment you press the dictation key, so polished text lands about a second sooner. Needs COS server 6.79.2 or later.
Answer with your own key (Settings, off by default, COS server 6.80.0 or later): paste an OpenRouter or Anthropic key, pick Claude Sonnet 5.5 or Claude Haiku 5.5, and set a daily cap ($1 to start).
The key is stored by the COS server on this Mac and never shown again: Control shows its kind and last four characters, and clears the clipboard after the paste.
Reset pause, Use for answers, Remove and Remove all keys are buttons, each confirmed first. Saved keys can still be removed after going back to an older COS.
Sessions that ran on a key cannot be continued, forked or opened in their app from Control, so they never resume on your plan.
New installs get an optional Add your own key step at the end of setup. Skip is the default and sends nothing.

Dictation: if your Mac misses the moment you let go of the dictation key, COS now notices and finishes the dictation normally, typing the text instead of copying it. If the 🌐 key also has a job in macOS, COS tells you and opens Keyboard settings. A press while the last dictation is still finishing now says so. Dictation settings now live in Activity, Dictation, Settings.
Dictation no longer quits COS Control when you switch to a microphone with a different audio format, like the Studio Display Microphone.
Your pet and the listening pill stay smooth while dictation starts: the microphone, the start sound and Mute other apps now start in the background.
A dictation that caught no speech says so, instead of reporting an error and offering a Retry that cannot help.
AI polish records why it did or did not run (daily cap, busy, too long, off, failed) in the dictation timing file, so a skipped polish is never silent.
Memories, Cues to rate: the last 7 days of live cues one at a time, oldest first, with the meeting, the time, the kind, the score, its sources and what was said just before it.
Rate each one Useful, Late, Repeat, Wrong or Obvious. Keys 1 to 5 rate, N adds a note and S skips, while the cue card is selected.
Memories, Rated cues: the cues you rated in the last 7 days, with their verdicts and notes. Pick another verdict to change one, or Clear it.

Meetings: a Cues view beside Live COS Ask lists the meeting's cues, newest first, with the verdicts inline and how many of the meeting's cues are used. It refreshes every 15 seconds while it shows. Saved glasses meetings show their cues too.
Your up and down votes on the glasses still count and are kept beside your verdict.
Needs COS server 6.79.0. On an older server none of this shows.

Dictation keeps your last word. When you let go of the key (or press Start / stop again), COS keeps listening for 300 milliseconds, so the end of what you said is not cut off. You no longer need to hold the key longer.
The pill keeps showing LISTENING for that moment, and the stop sound plays only after the microphone closes, so it is never in the recording.
Press the key again within that moment and the same dictation carries on. Nothing is lost and nothing from two dictations is mixed.
Cancel, sleep and the two-minute limit still stop at once.

Each dictation now adds one line of numbers to dictation-timing.jsonl in COS Control's Application Support folder: how long the microphone stayed open after you let go, the speech level just before and after, the engine, how long transcription took, and AI polish's model, result and time. Never your words or audio. It is the place to look when a dictation seems cut off. The file stays under 512 KB.
AI polish (Settings, Dictation): Off, Claude Haiku or Claude Sonnet. Off is the default.

With a model chosen, Claude cleans each dictation before COS pastes it: filler words like um, punctuation, doubled words and spellings from your COS dictionary. It does not reliably fix a word the speech engine misheard, and Sonnet sometimes guesses wrong.
The pill says POLISHING while Claude works. COS waits at most 5 seconds for Haiku and 9 for Sonnet; if Claude is slower, unavailable or fails, COS pastes what it heard, with no error card.
Uses your Claude plan through the COS server, with the server's own daily limit. Dictations over 8,000 characters are pasted as heard.
Dictation history marks a polished dictation Polished · Haiku or Polished · Sonnet, and its detail shows What was heard, with Copy.

Jedi Miles Windu, the default pet, now fights shuffled opponent casts like Nia, Elara and Rowan: two, three and four sessions each rotate three casts without an immediate repeat, and one session keeps the slower sprint.
A Miles Windu pet that was never changed updates by itself. A pet you changed or installed yourself stays exactly as it is.
Use on a shipped character now needs a click: Return no longer confirms it, and a confirm left open is withdrawn when the panel closes, so a stray key cannot replace your pet.
Nia, Elara and Rowan defend with their sabers before striking. Opponents react after contact, with clearer follow-through and a smoother return to guard.
Two-, three- and four-session encounters shuffle three opponent casts without an immediate repeat. The cast approaching at the end stays for the next encounter.
Grounded opponents stay on the floor; flight-capable droids make the aerial approaches. Existing custom artwork and timing remain yours.
Before COS types a dictation, it reads the words already in the text box, so a name or term written there comes out spelled the same way. If the box says Ukaoma, a dictated Ukoma is typed as Ukaoma.

When you fix a dictated word to a spelling the same text box already has, such as a name in a prompt you pasted, Learn from my edits takes it even when it sounds less alike. Its suggestion says why: Also in the text around your dictation.
COS keeps that text only for the one dictation and never saves or sends it. Never in terminals or password fields. Turn it off in Settings, Dictation: Spell words the way the text box has them.
If COS Control does not close for an update within 20 seconds, the update closes it and reopens the new version. You no longer need Force Quit.
A Mac recording is never cut off: the update stops, says "Finish the Mac recording, then choose Try again", and installs nothing until you do.
While it installs, the window says "Closing COS Control…", then the new version opens.
If an update could not close COS Control, the next launch offers Finish installing, with nothing to download again.
A Live cues switch in Settings, in the Meeting assistant card under Home city. Turn live cues on or off here; nobody edits the server's files by hand.
The line under the switch says what cues use, like On. Cues use Claude Sonnet 5.5, SubQ, and your notes. Or what stops them, in words, and what to do.
Needs a Jev or SubQ key comes with Add a Jev or SubQ key, which opens Decision models where the key fields are.
Turned on in the server's environment shows the switch on and held. An older server says Needs server 6.76.2, and an unreachable server says so instead of showing the last answer.
Cues also need Live Cues on in the glasses app. Needs server 6.76.2 and COS Glasses 6.10.644.
Stop and save a glasses meeting from COS Control. It is in the live meeting header, and in the panel when one glasses meeting is recording. Confirm, and COS asks the glasses to stop.
The glasses stop and save the meeting themselves, so the lens shows Saving and Saved and no audio is split into a second meeting.
COS says what happened: Saving the meeting, then Saved with its name. If the glasses are not connected, the server is unreachable or the meeting already stopped, it says so and nothing stops.

Meeting Ask’s copied context shows where in the meeting each answer reached, as Through 3:30, and how long the answer took when the server measured it, as Answer time: 6.4 s. It no longer prints a meeting position in milliseconds that read like a wait.
Needs COS Glasses 6.10.644 and server 6.76.1.

Download and install finishes on its own. COS Control asked itself to quit in a way that could stall forever, so the window sat on Installing while a normal quit worked. It now quits, installs and reopens.

Updating to 0.5.320 from an older version can still stall once, because the old version runs the install. If Installing has not finished after a minute, Force Quit COS Control (Option-Command-Escape): the update then installs and reopens it.
Quit in the menu bar panel uses the same reliable path.
Old update downloads are removed when a new one starts, so the updates folder keeps only the one being installed.
Download and install shows real progress, for example Downloading 30.0 of 137.2 MB, about 55 s left.
Installing says it usually takes under a minute. If a Mac recording is still saving, it says COS Control is saving it first.

Installing can no longer hang. If COS Control has not closed after 75 seconds, the window says why nothing was installed (for example, finish your meeting first) and offers Try again. The same reason shows once if COS Control reopens on the old version.
The update download no longer fails on slower connections. It stops only if no data arrives for a minute.
These improvements apply to updates after this one: the window that installs an update belongs to the version being replaced.

Allow in a dictation card opens the exact Accessibility page with the COS bar to drag COS Control in, and the card closes once it works. Already on but not working? Reset and add again removes the old entry and asks macOS again.

Mute other apps, Mac recording and the quiet-mode note ask macOS for System Audio Recording, so COS Control appears in that list. If it was refused before, the COS bar opens the page to drag it in. Until it is allowed, COS lowers the volume instead and recording carries on.
The setup guide's Voice check no longer reports "No speech detected" on a working Mac. Its test clip repeated one sentence, which the server discards as a loop; it now sends one sentence.
Miles Windu lightsaber is the dictation sound for every Jedi pet, not only Jedi Miles Windu. A sound you picked yourself stays as it is.

sections.title: Dictation for everyone
items: Dictation works with Whisper too. Settings, Transcription, Dictation engine: Automatic (recommended), Parakeet Ultra or Whisper. Automatic uses Parakeet Ultra when it is installed and ready, and Whisper on this Mac otherwise. Dictation never uses the cloud.

Install Parakeet (654 MB) from Settings, the menu bar or a dictation card. COS Control now includes the speech tool Parakeet needs, so there is no Terminal step. Progress and Cancel show while it downloads, every file is checked, and dictation keeps working with Whisper meanwhile.

When a dictation cannot be transcribed, the card says why and offers the one thing that fixes it: Install Parakeet, Use Whisper, Retry, or Open Transcription settings. Retry appears only when it can work.

The setup guide has a Dictation engine step after Voice. Test on this Mac dictates a 30 second sample with each installed engine and shows its speed and how many words it got wrong. It is a quick check, not a full accuracy test. Voice turns green only once a real test dictation works.
Dictation history shows which engine transcribed each dictation.
Whisper dictation and the Parakeet install need server 6.74.0. An older server keeps Parakeet-only dictation, as before.

Work chat no longer stops at "Earlier handoffs need a check first". COS plans anyway, and when you send, the round queues behind the earlier work and sends by itself once that work is done, reviewed, or answered. The card says what it waits for, with Cancel.

Settings, Work, When earlier work is still open: Queue it (the default) or Ask each time. Ask each time offers Queue it, Send in parallel (free sessions now; a busy session gets its part after its own work) or Check first.
Plan and send queues too; it never skips the check. Queued work sends while COS Control is open, and waits while it is closed. Needs server 6.73.15; an older server keeps the check first.

Fixed: a card could keep saying Earlier handoffs need a check first, with Check again greyed out, while COS wrote its update summary. Check again, Plan and Send now stay available, and a message you send goes right after that summary.
The Work board has a Complete column again, after QA. Drop a card there to mark it complete (COS asks once), or drag it out to reopen it. The latest completions come first.
Opening a card with many sessions now says Loading 8 sessions, and Work chat shows its history as soon as it can, instead of looking empty for a few seconds.

Link a session to other tasks as a reference: in Link existing session, choose Link as reference, even for a session already working on another task. References sit in their own group on the card with Open and Unlink. COS uses their summary, outputs and changes as context there, never sends to them from that task, and they never change its stage.

Fix a word now fixes the dictation itself: Heard shows your spelling as soon as you save. Replace it in now works in Claude, Slack and other Electron apps, by pasting the corrected words over exactly the text COS typed. When COS can't prove that text is still there, it copies the fix and tells you what to do.

Format spoken lists (Settings, Dictation, on by default): say "number one, number two" or "bullet, next bullet" and COS writes a numbered or bulleted list, one item per line. Ordinary sentences with numbers in them stay as they are.

Learn from my edits (Settings, Dictation): when you fix a word COS just typed, in that same field, COS learns it. Save automatically is the default, with Undo in Recent corrections. Suggest only keeps suggestions for a week so you can add them in a batch. Native apps for now; Claude, Slack and other Electron apps are measured first. Never in terminals or password fields.
COS Activity has a new Dictation tab: suggested and learned corrections with Undo, recent corrections, your latest dictations, the full history and the dictionary.
Miles Windu moves more naturally: faster droid entrances, no frozen stance, smoother deflections.
Fixed: While dictating, Mute other apps left music and video playing (0.5.313 and 0.5.314). COS's own start and stop sounds still play.
If COS can't mute, it lowers the volume instead, and Settings says so under While dictating.
New dictation sound: Miles Windu saber. It's the default for the Jedi Miles Windu pet.
Fixed: COS Control quit as soon as a dictation start or stop sound finished playing (0.5.313).
While a meeting records, on this Mac or the glasses, the pet shows a REC pill. Click it to open the live meeting.

sections.title: Fix dictation faster
items: Fix a dictation the moment it lands: Fix on the pill for 5 seconds, or ⌃⌥F (set in Settings).
Click, drag and move windows while you hold the dictation key: COS keeps listening, and the text lands where your cursor ends up. A click right after the press is still ⌥-click or ⌘-click.

If a dictation is cut short (another key while you hold the shortcut, or sleep), COS still transcribes what you said and copies it; a card shows the text with Copy. If you copied something meanwhile, your clipboard is left alone. Under a second is dropped.
After you fix a word, Replace it in the app puts the corrected text back where COS typed it, when that spot hasn't changed; otherwise COS copies the corrected text.
Fix a word selects the whole misheard phrase and suggests the spelling from your dictionary. Return saves.
Other apps go quiet while you dictate and come back after (Settings, While dictating: Mute, Lower or Off). Never while COS is recording, on this Mac or the glasses.

sections.title: Meetings on the Mac
items: When Zoom, Teams or Google Meet starts using your microphone, the pet offers Record. One click records all Mac audio with a title like "Zoom meeting 2:00 PM". COS never records or stops on its own; for a recording started from that card, it asks before stopping once the meeting app lets go of the mic.
Record on Mac is one click: the first recording shows a short COS notice once, then Record just starts. While recording, COS reminds you to let people know.
Open live meeting now opens the live transcript. With a glasses meeting and a Mac recording live at once, switch between them from the top of the live view.

Saved Mac recordings now appear in Meetings, and the live view opens them when saving finishes (needs server 6.73.14). The no-sound warning shows only while recording. If a recording stops on its own (the two-hour limit, sleep), COS tells you so you can start again.
In Settings: Suggest recording when a meeting starts (on or off), which apps to watch, apps you set to Never from the pet's card (remove them here), and Show the recording notice again.

sections.title: Smoother
items: COS Control uses much less CPU while the Work tab is open, so the pet animates smoothly.

sections.title: Work context meter
items: Each Work chat assignment shows what it will send, split by source, before you click Send. Open it to preview any item (Space opens Quick Look), remove it or add one that was left out.
The planner (server 6.73.13 or later) picks only what each assignment needs, and the round shows how much it sends of everything linked to the card.
Prefer not to review? Plan and send sends every assignment as soon as it is planned, through the same checks. Review stays the default; Send plans without review in Settings changes that.
Connections shows how full each linked session's context is, the files it wrote since your handoff, and its code changes, with Review changes.

sections.title: Dictation sounds and history
items: Start and stop sounds per pet: Unstable saber for the Jedi, chirps for droids, a chime for the rest, or any of eight original sounds or your own file (trimmed for you). Set pitch and volume in Settings.
After COS pastes, your clipboard comes back exactly as it was.
The listening waveform reads quiet USB microphones properly, and the pill appears on whichever screen you're typing on.
The DICTATIONS pill shows your latest 10; All dictations opens a searchable history. Keep dictations for 7, 30 (default) or 90 days, or forever; Clear dictation history asks first.

sections.title: Dictation, Wispr-style
items: Hold your shortcut and the bar under your pet becomes a listening pill with a live waveform that moves for quiet speech too. No window opens, and nothing takes focus from the app you are typing in. With the pet hidden, the same pill sits above the Dock.

Release and COS transcribes, copies the text, and drops it into whatever text box has your cursor when it finishes, so you can click somewhere else while it works. The pill flashes ✓ Inserted with the app's name only when COS sees the text land. The text stays on the clipboard, so ⌘V works again anywhere.

Some apps, such as terminals and Electron editors, get ⌘V; COS shows Pasted when it can't confirm. COS sends ⌘V once and never asks you to paste again; the text stays on the clipboard and in Recent dictations with Copy.
No text box selected? A card pops over the pet with the text and a Copy button. It folds away after 20 seconds; hover to keep it.
The DICTATIONS pill on the pet opens Recent dictations, kept on this Mac, each with where it went and a Copy button.
Still refused: password fields, and secure keyboard input held by another app (its own card). COS never presses Send or Return, and line breaks become spaces in a terminal.
Delete a dictation from its row, or clear them all in Settings.
Recent dictations on the pet shows only your dictations, without the running sessions under it.

sections.title: Dictionary
items: Open a dictation and choose Fix a word: tap what COS got wrong, type the right spelling, Save. It joins the one COS dictionary your G2 meetings, Mac recordings and dictation already use, from the next sentence on.
Recent corrections show what COS learned, from where and when, and each one can be undone.

Meetings → Dictionary in COS Activity shows the whole dictionary: recent corrections, vocabulary and every correction, searchable, with add and remove. Fix a word, Undo and single-word edits need server 6.73.12; on an older server the dictionary still reads and takes hand-added corrections.

sections.title: Dictate into any Mac app
items: Turn on Dictate into Mac apps in Settings, choose a microphone, and set Push to talk and Start / stop shortcuts. Speech runs through Parakeet Ultra on this Mac with your COS dictionary.
Any key can be the shortcut: a modifier plus a key, a function key, or one modifier key by itself such as Fn 🌐 or Right ⌘. Fn+arrow and other chords never start dictation.
To use Fn, set System Settings → Keyboard → Press 🌐 key to Do Nothing, and move Wispr Flow off Fn. Fn and single-key shortcuts use Accessibility, which insertion already needs.
A click right after you press your shortcut modifier (⌥-click, ⌘-click) counts as a chord and never starts dictation; later clicks keep dictating.

sections.title: Manual Mac recording
items: Choose Record on Mac in Meetings and press Record (a short notice the first time). All Mac audio is the default: it records whatever app plays the call, without picking one. Your microphone is not recorded; glasses are optional.
Open live meeting shows the transcript as it arrives, with COS Ask and meeting files, the same view as a glasses recording.
Live COS Ask opens Mac recordings, with server 6.73.9.
The panel checks every chunk for sound. If nothing reaches COS for 12 seconds it says so, instead of only counting chunks received.

A red menu bar indicator and Stop control stay available while recording. Local audio is retained for explicit recovery if delivery is interrupted; a silent capture can be kept while you record again.
Work requests blocked before sending can be reviewed and sent to another connected session, or a new or forked session, after confirmation.
A Mac recording that stopped while its audio still uploads reads "Capture stopped · saving N/M" on Meetings, with Finish saving, instead of Live now.

sections.title: A focused welcome
items: Start with Just my Mac, or add Even G2 glasses as an optional setup step. The existing COS design and setup components stay familiar.
Resume unfinished setup after relaunch. Provider and Mac readiness checks remain in place, and existing installations keep their settings.

sections.title: Choose your decision provider
items: Choose Jev or optional SubQ Snap Preview in Settings, with separate overrides for session recommendations, completion suggestions and work search. Jev stays the default.
Save your SubQ key securely in the local server configuration. Responses identify their actual provider; a provider failure does not silently switch accounts.
SubQ is a public preview. Enabling it sends the selected workflow context to SubQ under its retention policy.

sections.title: Selected local transcription
items: Voice setup shows your selected and available transcription engines. A selected Parakeet configuration keeps its choices and does not offer the legacy Whisper tier installer.
Manual Mac recordings use the selected saved-meeting engine for canonical text. When Parakeet is selected and unavailable, captured audio stays available for retry.

sections.title: Continue the conversation
items: A completed native turn can accept a follow-up after an exact reply and fresh idle evidence are checked. User review and shared task completion remain separate.
Uncertain deliveries and active sessions keep their protection against duplicate sends.
A request refused before sending is labeled Not sent. Use this request again restores its text without dispatching it. Historical missing receipts require a session check.
Send explains when receipt refresh is in progress.

sections.title: One Control at a time
items: Opening another signed copy brings the running Control forward. The installed app can close an old rollback copy with a normal quit.
Updates keep rollback copies outside Applications and register the installed app for future launches. Server state and model choices stay unchanged.

sections.title: Responsive typing
items: Typing updates only the composer. Chat history and file lists stay separate.
Drafts save after a short pause and immediately when you send or leave the view.
Background receipt refreshes keep the editor available.
Context to send, Add task, replies and review titles keep typing local to their editors.

sections.title: Tasks from meetings
items: Create a task from a saved meeting, choose its domain, then open it in Work.
The task keeps its source meeting and saved meeting files. Existing task linking remains available.

sections.title: Work chat
items: Describe an outcome and COS drafts assignments for linked sessions. Nothing is sent until you review it: send each one, edit its prompt, skip it, or Send all. Not now keeps them as drafts.
Choose Opus or Sonnet to plan, beside the composer. Opus is the default; the choice stays on this Mac. Needs server 6.73.10; older servers plan with Sonnet.
If an earlier handoff on the card is still unresolved, COS lists it first, with Mark reviewed, Acknowledge or Check status, instead of refusing partway through a plan.
A refused assignment shows its reason and the others stay sendable. If the task, its files or its sessions change after planning, COS asks you to plan again.
Read each session’s delivery status and results together in the task conversation. Shared task completion remains your decision; Cursor and app-owned sessions keep manual continuation.
Choose how hard the planner thinks: Low, Medium or High (default). Each round names the model and effort that planned it, and says Dispatched only when a session received an assignment.

sections.title: Rich task context
items: Format Work chat with bold, italic, headings and lists. Drafts keep their formatting when you return.
Drop or paste images and media into task attachments. Native assignments carry the saved files and readable companions.

sections.title: Close a live recording
items: A Live now row that has had no audio for two minutes offers End and save. It saves everything the server received; audio the glasses or phone still hold is not added after that.
A stopped recording whose upload paused says so, with Finish saving.

sections.title: Known limitations (field test)
items: Mac recording stops at two hours in this pilot.
The meeting-to-Work intake job still uses Jev on its schedule; the SubQ choice covers Work search, session suggestions and completion checks.
The dictation crash fix and Ask on Mac recordings are confirmed in the field test, not yet in this build.

notice.title: If an update sits on Downloading or Installing
notice.body: COS Control 0.5.318 and earlier can stop partway through downloading an update, because the update is now about 400 MB. If Downloading has not finished after two minutes, download COS Control from gotcos.com/control, unzip it and move it into Applications, replacing the old copy. COS Control 0.5.319 and earlier can also stall while installing: when the window says Installing, Force Quit COS Control (Option-Command-Escape) within a minute, and the update installs and reopens. Your meetings and the glasses server are not affected. From 0.5.320 on, updates install by themselves.
